ENGLISH — PREMIUM REVISION PAPER #11
====

GRADE: Grade 7
SUBJECT: ENGLISH
TIME ALLOWED: 2 hours 30 minutes
TOTAL MARKS: 100
EXAM BODY: KJSEA

INSTRUCTIONS
----
1. Answer all questions.
2. For calculations, show formula → substitution → steps → final answer with units.
3. For multiple choice, choose the best option.
4. Check your work before submitting.

SECTION A — MULTIPLE CHOICE
----
1. A noun is a word that names: (1 mark)
   A. Only a joining word
   B. Only a describing word
   C. A person, place, thing, or idea
   D. Only an action

2. A paragraph should usually have: (1 mark)
   A. Only one word repeated
   B. No full stops
   C. Many unrelated topics with no link
   D. One main idea with supporting sentences

3. When practising Reading 2.2.1 Intensive reading: Simple poems, which approach is best? (1 mark)
   A. Avoid reading anything related to Reading 2.2.1 Intensive reading: Simple poems.
   B. Copy random text without understanding Reading 2.2.1 Intensive reading: Simple poems.
   C. Use clear examples, correct form, and a short local context for Reading 2.2.1 Intensive reading: Simple poems.
   D. Use insults to “practise” Reading 2.2.1 Intensive reading: Simple poems.

4. The past tense of “go” is: (1 mark)
   A. goes
   B. went
   C. goed
   D. going

5. When practising Writing 1.5.1 Handwriting: Legibility and Neatness, which approach is best? (1 mark)
   A. Use insults to “practise” Writing 1.5.1 Handwriting: Legibility and Neatness.
   B. Avoid reading anything related to Writing 1.5.1 Handwriting: Legibility and Neatness.
   C. Copy random text without understanding Writing 1.5.1 Handwriting: Legibility and Neatness.
   D. Use clear examples, correct form, and a short local context for Writing 1.5.1 Handwriting: Legibility and Neatness.

6. When practising Grammar in Use 1.3.1 Word Classes: Nouns, which approach is best? (1 mark)
   A. Copy random text without understanding Grammar in Use 1.3.1 Word Classes: Nouns.
   B. Avoid reading anything related to Grammar in Use 1.3.1 Word Classes: Nouns.
   C. Use insults to “practise” Grammar in Use 1.3.1 Word Classes: Nouns.
   D. Use clear examples, correct form, and a short local context for Grammar in Use 1.3.1 Word Classes: Nouns.

7. When practising Listening and Speaking 1.1.1 Conversational Skills: Polite Language, which approach is best? (1 mark)
   A. Avoid reading anything related to Listening and Speaking 1.1.1 Conversational Skills: Polite Language.
   B. Copy random text without understanding Listening and Speaking 1.1.1 Conversational Skills: Polite Language.
   C. Use clear examples, correct form, and a short local context for Listening and Speaking 1.1.1 Conversational Skills: Polite Language.
   D. Use insults to “practise” Listening and Speaking 1.1.1 Conversational Skills: Polite Language.

8. Choose the correctly punctuated sentence. (1 mark)
   A. Where is the Library
   B. where is the library
   C. Where is the library?
   D. Where is the library

9. Which word is a verb? (1 mark)
   A. blue
   B. run
   C. happiness
   D. quickly

10. When practising Grammar in Use 2.3.1 Word Classes: Nouns, which approach is best? (1 mark)
   A. Avoid reading anything related to Grammar in Use 2.3.1 Word Classes: Nouns.

   D. Use clear examples, correct form, and a short local context for Grammar in Use 2.3.1 Word Classes: Nouns.

   B. Avoid reading anything related to Writing 2.5.1 Mechanics of Writing: Punctuation Marks.

   D. Use clear examples, correct form, and a short local context for Writing 2.5.1 Mechanics of Writing: Punctuation Marks.

14. When practising Reading 1.4.1 Intensive Reading: Trickster Narratives, which approach is best? (1 mark)

   B. Avoid reading anything related to Reading 1.4.1 Intensive Reading: Trickster Narratives.

25. In three clear sentences, explain Reading 8.2.1 Intensive Reading and give one Kenyan example. (4 marks)
